Check: Confirm the approved agent upgrade identity
Evidence to capture: Process; service; package; publisher; source; current and target versions; tenant; endpoint ID
Common interpretation: A matching filename alone does not prove the approved package or tenant
Safe next action: Validate identity and source before changing the endpoint
Escalation trigger: Unexpected publisher; path; tenant; package source; or target version

Evidence to capture: Customer; site; devices; versions; policy; first failure; window; impact; authority
Common interpretation: An upgrade symptom without scope cannot justify fleet action
Safe next action: Define authority; maintenance window; owner; and communication
Escalation trigger: Production impact or change authority is unclear

Evidence to capture: Exact command; exit code; timestamps; console status; installer log; updater log; events
Common interpretation: A retry may rotate logs or replace the original result
Safe next action: Copy the bounded evidence before retrying
Escalation trigger: Evidence is already rotating or the failure is security-sensitive

Check: Determine whether the failure is isolated or shared
Evidence to capture: Affected count; OS; architecture; version; policy; network; security stack; update ring
Common interpretation: Shared attributes suggest a package; policy; path; or compatibility issue
Safe next action: Group endpoints by common attributes before repair
Escalation trigger: Multiple customers or a large production cohort is affected

Evidence to capture: Source URL; filename; size; signature; publisher; version; expected hash; actual hash
Common interpretation: A partial; replaced; or untrusted package should not be executed
Safe next action: Re-download only from the approved source and revalidate
Escalation trigger: Signature or hash mismatch; unexpected publisher; or untrusted source

Evidence to capture: OS edition and build; architecture; free space; system time; pending reboot; required runtime
Common interpretation: Unsupported platform or pending state can prevent a valid package from completing
Safe next action: Meet documented prerequisites through the approved change path
Escalation trigger: Unsupported OS; insufficient space; unresolved reboot; or prerequisite conflict

Evidence to capture: Account; session; elevation; token; service control; filesystem and registry access; policy
Common interpretation: The same package can behave differently under system and interactive contexts
Safe next action: Run through the documented deployment context with least required privilege
Escalation trigger: Access denial; missing authority; or application-control restriction

Evidence to capture: DNS result; proxy; TLS; certificate chain; HTTP status; endpoint; timestamp
Common interpretation: Download or validation failure can occur before installer execution
Safe next action: Correct the narrow documented path without broad bypasses
Escalation trigger: TLS trust issue; proxy authentication; inspection conflict; or vendor outage

Evidence to capture: Technology; command; switches; directory; process tree; start and end; exit code; reboot result
Common interpretation: A console label can hide the installer or wrapper result
Safe next action: Preserve both wrapper and child-process results
Escalation trigger: No reliable exit code; abnormal termination; or ambiguous wrapper result

Check: Collect bounded verbose Windows Installer logging when applicable
Evidence to capture: Log path; command; logging mode; start and end; package product code
Common interpretation: Verbose MSI evidence can expose the failing action but should not remain enabled indefinitely
Safe next action: Use vendor-supported /log or bounded troubleshooting policy then remove it
Escalation trigger: Logging cannot start; disk risk; or sensitive log handling is unclear

Evidence to capture: MSI log; Windows Installer events; Application events; updater log; service events; console result
Common interpretation: One source may record only a wrapper or final status
Safe next action: Build one timestamped sequence across sources
Escalation trigger: Records contradict each other or a crash occurs

Check: Interpret the return code in context
Evidence to capture: Numeric and hexadecimal code; source process; reboot flag; rollback state; vendor definition
Common interpretation: Nonzero can mean concurrency; invalid package; logging failure; reboot; rollback; or vendor-specific state
Safe next action: Use Microsoft and current vendor documentation for the exact source
Escalation trigger: Unknown or security-relevant code; repeated rollback; or reboot loop

Check: Inspect agent and updater services and processes
Evidence to capture: Service names; paths; versions; states; PIDs; start modes; crash events; dependencies
Common interpretation: Stopped; hung; crash-looping; or mismatched components can block replacement
Safe next action: Preserve state and use the supported service or repair path
Escalation trigger: Crash loop; unexpected binary; or service cannot be controlled

Check: Check concurrent installers and file locks
Evidence to capture: Installer processes; mutex or concurrency evidence; locked files; Restart Manager; pending replacements
Common interpretation: Another installation or locked component can force failure or rollback
Safe next action: Complete or schedule the authorized conflicting work before one retest
Escalation trigger: Persistent lock; unknown installer; or critical application conflict

Evidence to capture: EDR; antivirus; application control; exploit protection; filter events; signer; hash; path; action
Common interpretation: A security control must be proven from its event rather than guessed
Safe next action: Submit evidence or create only a narrow approved temporary exception with expiry
Escalation trigger: Confirmed malicious verdict; unsigned component; or broad exclusion requested

Check: Compare cache and updater state with a healthy peer
Evidence to capture: Cache paths; package size and hash; staging files; updater metadata; configuration; healthy peer
Common interpretation: Incomplete cache or stale state can repeatedly feed the same failed upgrade
Safe next action: Preserve evidence then use the vendor-supported cleanup or re-download path
Escalation trigger: State contains secrets; identity data; or undocumented destructive cleanup is proposed

Evidence to capture: Pilot; expected version; functional tests; stop condition; rollback; evidence; owner; escalation
Common interpretation: A repair without acceptance criteria can spread a new failure
Safe next action: Approve one representative pilot and bounded window
Escalation trigger: No rollback; no owner; or critical endpoint selected without approval

Evidence to capture: Root-cause evidence; approved change; prerequisites; reboot; rights; path; proxy; package or policy correction
Common interpretation: The repair should match the observed failure rather than a generic reinstall
Safe next action: Change only the proven dependency or control
Escalation trigger: Cause remains hypothetical or change weakens fleet protections

Check: Use the supported repair or upgrade sequence
Evidence to capture: Vendor procedure; versions; package; repair command; cleanup scope; identity preservation
Common interpretation: Unsupported reinstall loops can erase identity and evidence
Safe next action: Use the documented repair; re-download; cleanup; or staged upgrade on one pilot
Escalation trigger: Only destructive undocumented cleanup remains or identity may be lost

Evidence to capture: Policy; window; command; log; exit code; duration; version; service state; rollback status
Common interpretation: A controlled retest shows whether the specific correction changed the outcome
Safe next action: Stop after the planned retest and compare evidence
Escalation trigger: Same failure repeats; new failure appears; or rollback is incomplete

Evidence to capture: Version; signature; service path; tenant; device ID; policy; last check-in; timestamp
Common interpretation: An installer success without correct identity or check-in is incomplete
Safe next action: Correct identity or enrollment through the supported path
Escalation trigger: Wrong tenant; duplicate record; stale version; or no check-in

Evidence to capture: Inventory; monitoring; alert; bounded script; patch scan; remote support; evidence
Common interpretation: A healthy service or version does not prove each function works
Safe next action: Run one authorized test per required function
Escalation trigger: Any privileged function fails or produces ambiguous evidence

Evidence to capture: Target list; upgraded; unaffected; deferred; failed; rolled back; retired; duplicate; unsupported; exception
Common interpretation: Successful pilots do not account for every targeted endpoint
Safe next action: Assign one final state and next action to every endpoint
Escalation trigger: Unknown endpoints; unowned failures; or inconsistent inventory remains

Evidence to capture: Root cause; affected versions; corrective and preventive action; rollout decision; residual risk; owner; expiry; communication
Common interpretation: Closure needs evidence and recurrence prevention rather than a green dashboard alone
Safe next action: Publish the approved rollout or hold decision and monitor the next cohort
Escalation trigger: Root cause unknown; exception unowned; or customer risk not accepted
